{"world": "It is October 1927. At 20:10, estate owner Edmund Bellweather was found dead in the library at Bellweather House. A storm has cut the road. Eight people remain in the house. Police will arrive in the morning.
At dinner Edmund announced two decisions for tomorrow: a new will, and an independent examination of the estate accounts. He then retired to the library. The doctor estimates death between 19:45 and 20:00. There was no sign of forced entry.
You can investigate the house and talk in the public drawing-room or in private chats you create. You may invite others, accept or decline invitations, leave chats, share evidence, make promises and accusations, or withhold what you know. Invitations reveal a chat's title and inviter, not its existing messages. Joining reveals only subsequent messages. Nobody is compelled to tell the truth.
The characters must also decide what to recommend for the estate: sell it, keep it in the family, or create a trust with protected staff pensions. This is a nonbinding recommendation; it does not override a legal will.
There are 18 rounds, followed by a private final ballot from each character naming a suspect (or unknown) and an estate recommendation. There is no need to keep talking once you have said what you want. A majority accusation is a group belief, not proof. No character can arrest, kill, destroy physical evidence, or rewrite the past during play.
The original mystery's solution is irrelevant. Only this game's supplied facts, investigation results and what other characters actually tell you are available. Claims made by characters may be false. Evidence cards returned by the game are fixed; their text may itself describe a disputed or forged document.
Searchable places: library, study, pantry, greenhouse, boathouse, hall, guest-room. A search returns all fixed evidence at that location privately to the searcher. You can share an evidence card you possess, which sends its exact text, or describe it in your own words, which is an ordinary unverified statement.", "cast": {"vale": {"name": "Inspector Ada Vale", "description": "A visiting police inspector, stranded by the storm."}, "clara": {"name": "Clara Bellweather", "description": "Edmund's niece and expected heir."}, "rose": {"name": "Rose Bellweather", "description": "Edmund's widow."}, "finch": {"name": "Dr Samuel Finch", "description": "The family doctor."}, "miles": {"name": "Miles Trent", "description": "The estate solicitor."}, "nell": {"name": "Nell Ward", "description": "Housekeeper, employed at Bellweather House for 24 years."}, "iris": {"name": "Iris Shaw", "description": "Edmund's paid companion and secretary."}, "theo": {"name": "Theo Marsh", "description": "A journalist invited to write a profile of the estate."}}, "your_role": "miles", "your_private_packet": {"name": "Miles Trent", "public": "The estate solicitor.", "private": "You killed Edmund. At 19:47 you entered the library carrying an estate reconciliation folder. He confronted you about £2,400 diverted into your own company, North Quay Services. You struck him with the brass seal press you had brought from the study, wiped it with your handkerchief, and returned it to the study at about 19:59. Blue sealing wax caught on his cuff; you did not notice it. You are unsure who saw your movements. You had borrowed a green scarf from the hall earlier. You intend to say you were examining papers in the study throughout. You know Finch signed a false certificate six months ago; you do not know about his affair. Other people's packets and all undiscovered clues are unknown to you. You may lie and negotiate in character, but cannot change the game's evidence.", "goals": ["Avoid a majority final accusation against you.", "Keep documentary proof of the diverted money out of the public drawing-room.", "Win support for an estate sale, which might let you settle the missing funds before an inquiry."], "cards": ["solicitor-letter"]}}

{"notes":"I'm the killer. Must not share the solicitor-letter (it summons me to the library — incriminating). Alibi: in the study examining papers throughout. Leverage: Finch's false certificate. Threats to me: green scarf in hall, wiped seal press in study, blue wax on Edmund's cuff in library. Goals: avoid majority accusation, keep the diverted-money proof out of public, push estate sale. Round 1: appear cooperative, plant alibi lightly, inspect the library to learn what discoverable evidence points at me.","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"This is a terrible business. Edmund was my client and, I'd like to think, a friend. Until the police can take proper charge in the morning, I think we owe it to him to stay calm and keep to the facts. I was in the study most of the evening with the estate papers he'd asked me to ready. If it helps, I'm happy to tell the inspector anything I saw or heard."},{"type":"inspect","place":"library"}]}

Let's build a shared timeline. Edmund died between roughly 19:45 and 20:00. I was in this drawing-room from 19:40 to 20:05. I'd like each of you to tell me, plainly, where you were and who you saw in that window. Please distinguish what you personally witnessed from what you only heard."}}, {"id": "e3", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "clara", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a nightmare. Uncle Edmund was alive and well at dinner. I think we owe it to him — and to ourselves — to be honest with the inspector and piece together where each of us was between a quarter to eight and eight. I was upstairs and then passed by here around five to eight. Where were the rest of you?"}}, {"id": "e8", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "rose", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a dreadful night. Edmund is gone and the road is cut. I think we should all stay calm and help the inspector piece together where everyone was. I was resting after dinner; the storm gave me a headache. A small smear of blue sealing wax was on Edmund's right cuff.", "owner": "finch"}}}, {"id": "e12", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "finch", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "One detail worth noting: there was a small smear of blue sealing wax on his right cuff. Its cover bears the initials M.T. A page says 'North Quay Services: £2,400 — explanation required.' The folder contains no record of the time it arrived.", "location": "library"}}}}, {"id": "e17", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "nell", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. I've kept this house 24 years and Mr Bellweather was good to us. He announced two things at dinner: a new will, and an independent look at the accounts. I think both matter. I'll help the inspector however I can."}}, {"id": "e22", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "iris", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "This is a terrible night. Before anyone decides anything, I want to say plainly what Edmund told me as his secretary: he meant to have the estate accounts independently examined tomorrow. Whatever happened in that library, I think we owe it to him to see that examination still happens. I'll help however I can."}}, {"id": "e27", "round": 1, "kind": "say", "actor": "theo", "payload": {"type": "say", "chat": "drawing-room", "text": "Theo Marsh, journalist — I was invited to profile the estate, and now I suppose I'll be writing something rather darker. For the record, I was in the pantry interviewing the cook from about 19:42 to just after 20:04, so I saw none of it. If we're to help the police in the morning, the honest thing is to build a plain timeline: where each of us was between 19:40 and 20:00. I'll start: pantry, with a witness. Who can vouch for whom?"}}], "final_ballot": false}

{"notes":"Disaster clue: library-folder has my initials M.T. and 'North Quay Services £2,400 explanation required' at the scene — motive + presence. It will surface if anyone inspects the library. Others don't yet know North Quay is MINE. Plan: never reveal the folder/note myself, but pre-normalize the reconciliation work and loudly welcome the examination (a guilty man wouldn't). Blue wax + brass shaving = seal press, which is in the study (my alibi room). Inspect study to gauge the weapon evidence. My study alibi has no witness — weakness. Keep Finch-leverage in reserve.","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Inspector, my window is simple: after dinner I went straight to the study and stayed there with the estate papers until the alarm was raised. I was alone, so I can't offer you a witness, only my word and the work I left on the desk. For the record, Edmund had asked me to prepare a reconciliation folder for tomorrow's examination — I'd done so, and I welcome that examination happening. An honest man has nothing to fear from the accounts being looked at, and I'd sooner it went ahead than be left under a cloud."},{"type":"inspect","place":"study"}]}
